title: What is the highest common factor of each pair on a ladder?
description: Two ladders are built, one for three hundred and one hundred fifty, and one for six hundred thirty and seven hundred seventy. Each row is divided by a prime that goes into both numbers, and the divisors on the left are multiplied. Keeko doubts this and divides by three once too often.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide by a prime only when it goes into both numbers in the row, and multiply the divisors when no prime is shared. Watch for students who divide when only one of the two numbers can take the prime.

source: Use the ladders for 300 and 150, and for 630 and 770, to find the HCF in each case.
video_script.why: The child has seen one ladder and now builds two more, where each divisor must go into both numbers of its row.
video_script.substitution: Divide both numbers by a prime that goes into both, again and again, and multiply the divisors.
video_script.anchor: Two ladders of division rows drawn side by side, as in the book.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko divides sixty three and seventy seven by three, but three does not go into seventy seven.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factors are one hundred fifty and seventy
never_show: a divisor 3 written on the left of the row 63, 77
video_script.design: One idea: a divisor is used only when it goes into both numbers in the row. The two ladders stay side by side on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two pairs of numbers are given. The first pair is three hundred and one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The second pair is six hundred thirty and seven hundred seventy. We have to find the biggest number that divides both numbers of each pair.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which prime goes into both six hundred thirty and seven hundred seventy?

beats.on_screen: the two pairs and the empty ladders stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We divide by a prime, which is a number whose only factors are one and itself.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The divisor is written on the left, and the two answers are written in the next row.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>These rows, one below the other, are called a ladder.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The largest number that divides both numbers is called the highest common factor.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the pairs three hundred and one hundred fifty, and six hundred thirty and seven hundred seventy.

beats.on_screen: To find: the HCF of each pair, using ladders

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the highest common factor of each pair.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: ladder for 300, 150. 2 | 300, 150 gives 150, 75. 5 gives 30, 15. 5 gives 6, 3. 3 gives 2, 1. No common prime, so stop

marks.m1: the divisor 2 and the row 150, 75 are written
marks.m2: the divisor 5 and the row 30, 15 are written
marks.m3: the divisor 5 and the row 6, 3 are written
marks.m4: the divisor 3, the last row 2, 1 and a stop sign are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take the first pair and divide both numbers by two. That gives one hundred fifty and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Divide both by five, and we get thirty and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Divide both by five again to get six and three.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Divide both by three to get two and one. These share no prime, so the first ladder stops.

marks.m1: the divisors 2, 5, 5, 3 on the left are circled
marks.m2: they are joined by multiplication signs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the answer is made from the divisors on the left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We multiply two, five, five and three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: ladder for 630, 770. 2 | 630, 770 gives 315, 385. 5 gives 63, 77. 7 gives 9, 11. No common prime, so stop

marks.m1: the divisor 2 and the row 315, 385 are written
marks.m2: the divisor 5 and the row 63, 77 are written
marks.m3: the divisor 7, the last row 9, 11 and a stop sign are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, take the second pair. Both numbers end in zero, so divide by two. That gives three hundred fifteen and three hundred eighty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Both end in five, so divide by five to get sixty three and seventy seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seven goes into both, so divide by seven to get nine and eleven. These share no prime, so this ladder stops.

marks.m1: the divisors 2, 5, 7 on the left are circled
marks.m2: they are joined by multiplication signs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, again we take the divisors on the left.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We multiply two, five and seven.

marks.m1: the two answers, 150 and 70, are written and boxed
marks.m2: the check lines are written below

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The highest common factors are one hundred fifty and seventy.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred fifty goes into three hundred twice. Seventy goes into six hundred thirty nine times, and into seven hundred seventy eleven times.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the second ladder
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: a divisor 3 beside the row 63, 77 with 21, 77 below; 77 divided by 3 does not come out whole; the bubble is struck out and the ladder stops at 9, 11

marks.m1: Keeko's bubble shows a divisor 3 beside the row 63, 77
marks.m4: the ladder returns with the last row 9, 11 lit

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks we should divide by three again, because three goes into sixty three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But three does not go into seventy seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A divisor must go into both numbers of the row, or we cannot use it.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The ladder stops at nine and eleven, and the divisors stay two, five and seven.
